name: 12 Jyotirlinga
blurb: All twelve Jyotirlingas — Somnath to Grishneshwar — one shared guide per shrine, even when a site also sits on another circuit.
lede: Complete set of twelve Jyotirlinga temples. Kedarnath also appears in Chota Char Dham and Panch Kedar — same page, same facts.

name: 51 Shakti Peeth
blurb: Shakti Peethas from the popular pilgrimage enumeration across India and neighbouring lands — including Himalayan seats such as Surkanda Devi and Champawat’s Panchsagar.
lede: Where tradition places Sati’s sacred fragments. Scriptural lists vary (often 51, 52, or 108); TirthaYatra’s circuit includes Surkanda Devi (head) and Panchsagar Champawat among the Himalayan peethas. Overlaps with Jyotirlinga / Char Dham complexes share the same temple guide.

name: Char Dham
blurb: Adi Shankaracharya’s four cardinal dhams only: Badrinath, Dwarka, Puri, and Rameswaram — not the Uttarakhand Chota Char Dham.
lede: Exactly four seats. Kedarnath is not part of this circuit (see Chota Char Dham). Badrinath appears in both Char Dham and Chota Char Dham with the same guide.

name: Chota Char Dham
blurb: Uttarakhand’s Yamunotri, Gangotri, Kedarnath, and Badrinath — the classic Himalayan Char Dham yatra.
lede: Do not confuse with Adi Shankaracharya’s pan-India Char Dham. This circuit is the seasonal Uttarakhand pilgrimage.

name: Panch Kedar
blurb: Five Garhwal shrines of Shiva’s form after the Pandava legend — Kedarnath, Tungnath, Rudranath, Madhyamaheshwar, Kalpeshwar.
lede: Kedarnath is shared with Jyotirlinga and Chota Char Dham; the other four complete the Panch Kedar set.

name: Pancha Bhuta Sthalams
blurb: Earth, water, fire, air, and space — five South Indian Shiva temples of the elemental circuit.
lede: Complete five-temple set: Kanchipuram, Thiruvanaikaval, Tiruvannamalai, Srikalahasti, and Chidambaram.

name: Ashtavinayak
blurb: Maharashtra’s eight sacred Ganesha temples — the classic Ashtavinayak yatra around Pune.
lede: Complete eight-temple set in traditional Morgaon-start order. Ideal 2–3 day road circuit from Pune.

name: Modern Temples
blurb: Contemporary pilgrimage landmarks — Akshardham, ISKCON, and other living temples of the modern era.
lede: Open trail of newer or rebuilt sacred complexes that draw huge urban and international crowds.

name: Ramayana Trail
blurb: Temples and tirthas woven into Rama’s journey — growing trail, not a fixed count.
lede: Walk Ramayana geography through temples that preserve local memory of exile, devotion, and return.

name: Mahabharata Sites
blurb: Sites tied to the Mahabharata and Bhagavad Gita — open trail, not a fixed count.
lede: From Kurukshetra to Dwarka and quieter epic-linked tirthas.

name: Beyond India
blurb: Sacred sites beyond India’s borders linked by shared mythology.
lede: Nepal, Sri Lanka, and the Kailash–Manasarovar landscape.

name: Gujarat Char Dham
blurb: Gujarat’s classic four-seat yatra — Somnath, Dwarka, Ambaji, and Pavagadh Kalika.
lede: A compact state circuit loved by Gujarati pilgrims: sea-facing Jyotirlinga and Krishna dham, plus two powerful Shakti seats. Confirm seasonal crowds and trust notices before you travel.

name: Braj Yatra
blurb: Mathura–Vrindavan–Govardhan circuit of Krishna–Radha memory — janmabhoomi, banks, and lilasthal.
lede: Walk Braj through temple guides tied to Krishna’s childhood geography. Pair with the wider Krishna Lila trail for Dwarka, Guruvayur, and beyond.

name: Hanuman Trail
blurb: Hanuman temples across India — Salasar, Sankat Mochan, Jakhoo, Mahavir Mandir, and more.
lede: Open trail of Hanuman kshaetras for Tuesday–Saturday devotees and Ramayana travellers.

name: Krishna Lila Trail
blurb: From Braj and Dwarka to Guruvayur, Udupi, Pandharpur, Nathdwara, and Puri — living Krishna geography.
lede: Open trail of major Krishna–Radha–Vitthal–Jagannath seats beyond a single state.

name: Murugan Trail
blurb: Murugan / Subramanya temples of the South — Palani, Tiruchendur, Thiruparankundram, Kukke, and kin.
lede: Open Skanda–Murugan trail for Skanda Shashti and Tamil–Karnataka devotees (includes Kataragama memory via Sri Lanka listing where tagged).

name: Rama Kshaetra
blurb: Rama–Sita temples and exile-memory tirthas — Ayodhya, Bhadrachalam, Chitrakoot, Nashik, Orchha, and more.
lede: Deity-focused Rama circuit alongside the broader Ramayana Trail epic geography.

name: Narasimha Kshaetra
blurb: South & Deccan Narasimha temples — Ahobilam, Simhachalam, Yadagirigutta, and related caves.
lede: Fixed set of Narasimha guides currently on TirthaYatra — fierce compassion of the man-lion avatara.

name: Kerala Kshetram
blurb: Kerala’s great kshetrams — Sabarimala, Guruvayur, Padmanabhaswamy, Chottanikkara, Vadakkumnathan, and more.
lede: State trail for Onam-to-Mandala travellers: purity customs are strict — read dress and offering notes on each guide.

name: Rajasthan Tirtha
blurb: Rajasthan pilgrimage mix — Pushkar, Nathdwara, Salasar, Khatu Shyam, Karni Mata, Eklingji, and desert devis.
lede: Open state trail across Vaishnava, Shakti, and folk seats of Rajasthan.

name: Myth Story Tirthas
blurb: Temples most often linked from TirthaYatra’s short myth stories — useful for home puja + yatra pairing.
lede: Open circuit built from story↔temple links (Kashi, Ayodhya, Tirumala, Braj, Kurukshetra, and more).

name: Dattatreya Trail
blurb: Maharashtra–Karnataka Dattatreya kshaetras — Audumbar, Narsobawadi, Maniknagar, Akkalkot.
lede: Compact Datta trail for Thursday devotees and Guru–Datta seekers.

name: Sai Baba Trail
blurb: Shirdi and related Sai mandirs — living modern bhakti with classical humility.
lede: Open Sai trail centred on Shirdi with urban Sai mandirs currently in the catalog.
